registration.title: A hierarchical, time-weighted Poisson model refitted weekly
registration.what: Replace the model with the Dixon-Coles family: an attack and a defence for every club, shrunk to a level for its league, with older matches counting less, refitted every week.
registration.why: It is the standard published way to build a football model, and it had never been compared with production.
registration.how: One fit covers every competition; every seven days it is refitted on all earlier matches and predicts the next seven.
registration.hypothesis: A model built on separate attack and defence from the ground up predicts better than the Elo-like rank.

expected.evidence: The final period had been looked at by earlier diagnostics, so this is strong historical evidence and not a blind test.

registration.success_criteria: The research round's bar (experiments/research_frame/REGISTER.md): better by 0.002 on the final period, the 99.6% interval excluding zero, Brier agreeing, better in 2024/25 and 2025/26, no goal market worse by 0.0005, and 60% of competitions no worse.

events.label: Final period
events.meaningful: Worse than production, in every season and in 51 of 62 competitions.

events.reason: 0.0054 worse. The single rank is not the limitation.
